evidence: acli_cli_ops.py: `codec = AdfCodec(rich="cloud" in cutover_clients())` then `body_arg = json.dumps(codec.to_wire(codec.fit_outbound(body)))` — unconditional ADF serialization
rich_text_codec.py:62-66 `def to_wire(self, text): ... if self._rich: return adf.markdown_to_adf(text); return adf.text_to_adf(text)` — returns an ADF document even when rich=False
Prior code sent `body` = `_sanitize_comment(body)` (plaintext) to `--body` (removed in this diff)
Consumer: acli.py:396 `return acli_cli_ops.add_comment(jira_key, body, ...)` and backend.py:283 `self.transport.add_comment` — the live Cloud comment enactment path
advisory.finding: acli_cli_ops.add_comment now unconditionally sends the comment body as json.dumps(codec.to_wire(body)) (an ADF document) to `--body`, whereas it previously sent the sanitized plaintext string. Because AdfCodec.to_wire returns an ADF doc even when rich=False (cutover off), the `reconciler.rich_text_cutover` flag (ships 'off') does NOT gate the ADF-wrapping — it only selects markdown-vs-text within the ADF. Thus the Cloud comment wire shape changes for ALL deployments, including default-off ones, not just cutover-on ones as the docstring implies.
scenarios: A Cloud deployment running with rich_text_cutover=off (the shipped default) posts comments — the wire body flips from plaintext to json.dumps(text_to_adf(...))
